acceptance: Path 1, oracle review submitted on a batch PR: the oracle-review workflow run (job review-event, event pull_request_review) succeeds and its head_sha equals the PR head. The oracle-gate bridge run dispatches the gate for that PR. The dispatched oracle-gate (workflow_dispatch pr=N) run posts oracle-gate on the PR head, and that status's updated_at is later than the review's submitted_at. Run IDs are recorded.

Path 2, /oracle-review rejudge on a batch PR: record the oracle-verdict run's event, its workflow_run.head_sha against the PR head, and whether the bridge found the PR. Record whether oracle-gate was refreshed anyway through the review-submitted notification. State the decision for oracle-verdict-dispatch-gate-after-review-20261025: proceed if the verdict completion did not map to the PR, otherwise drop with this evidence.

Path 3, dismissal: record from GitHub's API behavior and docs whether the oracle's COMMENT reviews can be dismissed at all. If they cannot, record that the dismissed trigger covers only approvals and change requests, and update the design doc if it claims otherwise.
Path 4: make pr-rerun on a batch PR reruns failed CI jobs, or reports nothing to rerun. It never closes and reopens the PR.
Path 5: a batch PR whose head still carries old failed oracle-review check runs from before the cutover arms with make pr-arm. Non-required failures do not block it.
Each result above is recorded in this item's context with run IDs or URLs before finish.

description:
Problem: the cutover changes which events refresh the required oracle-gate. Unit tests cannot prove GitHub's event payloads behave as the design assumes: the head_sha of review-event runs, the bridge's develop pull request lookup, and the dispatched gate run. Advisor finding F3 is unverified: oracle-verdict runs started by an /oracle-review comment, a dispatch or the schedule may complete against develop's head SHA, so the bridge cannot map them to the pull request.

Outcome: recorded live evidence for each event path, and a recorded proceed-or-drop decision for oracle-verdict-dispatch-gate-after-review-20261025.

Decision gates:
1. Observe only pull requests opened by this batch, or with the owner's permission. Never post stand-ins, close and reopen, or dismiss another session's reviews. Do not fabricate oracle verdicts.
2. If any path fails, create a follow-up item with needs on this item, then mark this item blocked with the reason instead of finishing it.

Item guardrails: observation only, apart from at most one docs correction PR when observed behavior contradicts docs/internal/oracle-review-v2.md. Allowed triggers are the existing ones: an /oracle-review comment on this batch's own pull requests and gh workflow run oracle-gate.yml --ref develop -f pr=<n>.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests.
